correctness.rationale: The degree-ten squarefreeness is equivalent to a²≠1. Explicit coefficient Hasse–Witt matrix has determinant -a² and has H(0)H(0)^(3)=0 with rank 2. Quotients by two distinct tame involutions are genus two with displayed Dickson equations, and their norm/pullback isogeny has degree 16 prime to 3; its factors are rank-zero genus-two, hence supersingular. The a-number and finite-field counts follow. Standalone exact arithmetic tests over F3,F9,F27 corroborate algebra but are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Comparisons of exact branch tuple, parameter family, Hasse multiplicity and implication direction found no covering claim. Shaska (2003) is characteristic-zero normal-form work, Moonen (2010) and Li–Mantovan–Pries–Tang (2018) treat distinct special monodromy types, and Kudo–Harashita–Senda (2020) explicitly knows only the isolated exceptional supersingular example in an equivalent form; the new claim is a full coefficientwise classification and quotient/isogeny boundary. Residual risks of unindexed source and routine general Cartier formula remain.
residual_risks: Specialist hyperelliptic or Dieudonné-module literature might give an equivalent full family computation under different coordinates.
The rank and determinant portions follow standard Cartier–Manin coefficient formulas, so value depends on the complete boundary, its multiplicity, and the genus-two isogeny explanation.
Search indices and accessible scientific records cannot prove absolute historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: A complete intrinsic p-rank/Newton classification in a natural genus-four dihedral family: a rank-four-to-zero jump occurs at one *smooth* parameter, with a double Hasse divisor on the marked coordinate, simple after parameter involution, and a degree-16 genus-two factorization explaining the characteristic-three supersingular specialization. These are motivated moduli and arithmetic boundary invariants, not arbitrary sampling or re-proving isolated known existence.
